title: The central role of EMT in tumor progression: mechanistic drivers, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic horizons.
authors: Ramalingam, Prasanna Srinivasan; Ilma, Baby; Hussain, Md Sadique; Jakhmola, Vikash; Fatima, Rabab; Rana, Amita Joshi; Agrawal, Mohit; Ashique, Sumel; Mekala, Janaki Ramaiah; Arumugam, Sivakumar
one_liner_zh: 该文综述EMT在肿瘤进展中的机制、生物标志物与治疗策略，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a central plasticity program in cancer. It enables carcinoma cells to acquire migratory, invasive, immunomodulatory, and therapy-resistant phenotypes. As a result, EMT is a key driver of metastatic progression and poor prognosis. This overview summarizes recent mechanistic innovations across EMT-inducing transcription factors (SNAIL, SLUG, TWIST, ZEB) and their interactions with major signaling cascades, including TGF-beta/SMAD, Wnt/beta-catenin, Notch, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and Hippo (YAP/TAZ). Together, these cascades integrate cues from the TME to sustain partial/hybrid EMT states and maintain cancer stemness. We present a review of epigenetic and post-transcriptional regulation of EMT (DNA methylation, histone regulation, and non-coding RNAs) and their role in reversible states transitions and drug tolerance. The translational section highlights advance in biomarker development and limitations of the static, single-timepoint assays in capturing EMT dynamics. We describe the possibilities of longitudinal, multimodal assessment, such as liquid biopsy, spatial profiling, and integrative multi-omics, for real-time monitoring of EMT states. Moreover, we explore the therapeutic opportunities involving epigenetic regulators, RNA-based interventions, EMT-immune crosstalk target, and selected natural products that modulate EMT circuits. Lastly, we propose a precision-oncology model that can consolidate the use of EMT-state stratification (epithelial-predominant, hybrid-mesenchymal, mesenchymal-predominant), adaptive monitoring, and rational combination therapies (with immunotherapy, ferroptosis inducers, and targeted agents) to overcome metastasis and resistance. Taken together, positioning EMT as a continuous, druggable spectrum, over binary switch, allows patient stratification using biomarkers and supports the development of next-generation interventions to reduce the risk of metastasis and enhance long-term clinical outcomes.
abstract_zh: 上皮-间质转化（epithelial-mesenchymal transition, EMT）是癌症中的一个核心可塑性程序。它使癌细胞获得迁移、侵袭、免疫调节和治疗抵抗的表型。因此，EMT是转移进展和不良预后的关键驱动因素。本综述总结了EMT诱导转录因子（SNAIL、SLUG、TWIST、ZEB）及其与主要信号级联（包括TGF-beta/SMAD、Wnt/beta-catenin、Notch、PI3K/AKT/mTOR和Hippo（YAP/TAZ））相互作用的最新机制创新。这些级联共同整合来自肿瘤微环境（TME）的信号，以维持部分/混合EMT状态并保持癌症干性。我们回顾了EMT的表观遗传和转录后调控（DNA甲基化、组蛋白调控和非编码RNA）及其在可逆状态转换和药物耐受中的作用。转化部分强调了生物标志物开发的进展，以及静态、单时间点检测在捕捉EMT动态变化方面的局限性。我们描述了纵向、多模式评估的可能性，如液体活检、空间分析和整合多组学，用于实时监测EMT状态。此外，我们探讨了涉及表观遗传调控因子、基于RNA的干预、EMT-免疫串扰靶点以及调节EMT回路的选择性天然产物的治疗机会。最后，我们提出一个精准肿瘤学模型，该模型可整合EMT状态分层（上皮为主、混合间质、间质为主）、适应性监测和合理联合治疗（与免疫治疗、铁死亡诱导剂和靶向药物）以克服转移和耐药。总体而言，将EMT定位为一个连续的、可药物干预的谱系，而非二元开关，有助于通过生物标志物进行患者分层，并支持开发下一代干预措施，以降低转移风险并改善长期临床结局。
